newsitem.title: USA: Castle seen going to Trump, may become a Hard Rock.
newsitem.headline: Castle seen going to Trump, may become a Hard Rock.

text.p: Donald Trump looks set to win shareholder approval Monday for a plan to sell the debt-ridden Trump Castle to Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts Inc. and restyle it, possibly under the successful Hard Rock Cafe theme.

Sources familiar with the situation said Trump Hotels shareholders were expected to approve the $500 million acquisition of the Castle from Donald Trump at a special meeting on Monday in New York City.
Donald Trump currently owns the Trump Castle and holds 40 percent of the outstanding shares of Trump Hotels.
The sources also said Trump Hotels was expected to begin discussions with Rank Organisation Plc about renovating Castle into a casino resort sporting the successful Hard Rock Cafe theme.
"We are confident, based on conversations with institutional shareholders, that the acquisition will be approved," said one source familiar with the situation.
Trump Hotels agreed three months ago to exchange 5.837 million shares and $884,500 in cash for the Castle and assume $348 million in outstanding Castle obligations and debt.
The deal's value has fallen by $25 million as Trump Hotels stock has dropped from about $30 a share when the pact was unveiled to a recent trading range of about $25 a share.
With the shareholder approval, the Castle would become part of Trump's gaming empire composed of the Taj Mahal, Trump Plaza and a riverboat casino near Gary, Ind.

As for talks with Rank, sources close to Trump said "retheming" the Castle was a top priority once it is acquired. Rank has emerged as a likely partner because the two companies already are familiar with each other from the installation of a Hard Rock Cafe at the Trump Taj Mahal.
The Hard Rock Cafe at the Taj Mahal is scheduled to open in November.

Such an alliance also would be a competitive response to ITT Corp.'s agreement with Planet Hollywood to develop themed hotel/casinos in Atlantic City, Las Vegas and other resort areas, industry alysts said. ITT owns Caesar's Atlantic City.

"They are exploring alternatives to retheme the Castle and among those being considered is the Hard Rock, a Trump's marina with a modern nautical theme, or other concept that appeals to a new, younger demographic," a source close to Trump said.
A Trump spokeswoman declined to comment and a spokesman at the Hard Rock's U.S. operations based in Orlando, Fla., said "there is no foundation" to the Castle speculation.

Analysts have said they expect Atlantic City's fortunes to brighten under looser state regulations, a building boom that will add much-needed hotel capacity, and the entrance of Mirage Resorts Inc. as the lead developer of the 178-acre "H" tract in the city's marina district.

Including the Mirage/Circus Circus project, there are expected to be a total of 8,900 new rooms in Atlantic City by 1999, on top of the 9,700 rooms there at the end of 1995, according to a recent Bear Stearns & Co. report.
Trump Hotels went public in May 1995.
